speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: First, we will amend the Act to allow the Valuation Review Board, in the absence of any member of the Board due to resignation, illness or any other cause, to continue to hear and determine the appeal if the parties consent and there are at least two remaining members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: This change will provide greater convenience to appellants, and mirrors existing provisions for the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Board of Review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Similar provisions will also be enacted for the Income Tax Board of Review through the Income Tax (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The amendment will apply to all appeals held before the Board after the Bill is gazetted, and also to appeals, the hearing of which has begun before the gazette date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Second, we will amend the Act to provide clarity and enhance the information gathering powers of the Comptroller of Property Tax, the Chief Assessor and the officers authorised by them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The amendment will allow the Comptroller of Property Tax, the Chief Assessor and their authorised officers to require persons to attend personally before them, to provide information at a time and place specified by them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The change will allow the Comptroller of Property Tax, the Chief Assessor and their authorised officers to require any person to be examined orally and provide information for investigation, if the person appears to know of the facts or circumstances concerning the person’s or another person’s properties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The change will also allow the Comptroller of Property Tax, the Chief Assessor and their authorised officers to reduce to writing any statements provided by persons who are required to provide information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Moreover, the change will enhance the penalties for failure to comply with a request for information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Lastly, we will amend the Act to provide a regulatory framework to implement an opt-out approach for digital property tax notices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The current provisions of the Act require taxpayers to provide specific consent before the Comptroller can issue them with digital tax notices instead of hardcopy notices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The widespread use of computers and mobile devices allows taxpayers to receive digital instead of hardcopy tax notices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: The use of digital notices gives taxpayers greater convenience, security and timeliness of alerts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: This is part of our move to being a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Taxpayers who wish to continue receiving hardcopy notices can opt out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
text: Taxpayers will thus have the flexibility to manage their preference for hardcopy or electronic (e)-copy at any time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The first potential hurdle is if the notices are not in our four official languages.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second potential hurdle is how to opt out.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, people will be able to opt out not just online.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: People should be able to opt out over the phone, counter, snail mail and so on, and in multiple languages, too.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Let us imagine someone, let us call her Mrs Lim, who does not understand English.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If she does not understand the notice or does not know how to go online to opt out, then we automatically stop her hardcopy notices, obviously she will miss her payments.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even for users who use the Internet, there are issues.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Where does the onus lie if a Notice for Payment from IRAS lands in the spam folder or the recipient is not aware of it, or just simply did not receive it?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, an officer from the Land Transport Authority asked me, "Dr Lee, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) officers sent you three emails, you did not reply at all.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Was it because you were not happy with them?" But when I checked, I really did not receive three emails from URA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is why I changed my email lately.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, a missed notice can result in a fine.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But should the taxpayer be held responsible in this instance?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, how does one know when receiving a notification that it is a genuine notice from IRAS, and not sent by someone to commits fraud?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Through the media, IRAS has highlighted attempts by people to commit fraud, to infect computers with virus through fake notices.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, this is a problem not only with IRAS, but there are many other agencies, too, as well as telecom companies like Singtel.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But we need to have a system in place to be smart enough to allow our computer systems to differentiate the fake from the real.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   IRAS is going to make digital notices the default mode of notification whereby Singaporeans must choose to opt-out in order to continue to receive hardcopy notices.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even Singaporeans who use the Internet regularly may encounter problems.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If the digital notice goes into their spam folder and ends up being automatically deleted after one month, will they be fined?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another question is whether this will result in more fraudsters pretending to be from IRAS.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: While I support the Bill, I would like to flag out some concerns regarding the third objective of the Bill, which is the serving of notices via electronic means.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: As Members of Parliament (MPs), we all know about the presence of the aged, frail and the vulnerable among our communities.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They frequently do not speak English, let alone read English or access the Internet.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Some of them are also in a poor state of mental health.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And some of them live alone without close family support.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: They do not form a large part of Singapore, but they do exist.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Also, as MPs, from time to time, we sometimes write appeals for residents who face legal issues because they do not pay their bills or fines to the Government in time due to their misunderstanding of the Government's communications, or their inability to use digital channels effectively.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Once they get themselves into such difficulties, they face additional fines and even legal worries.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Going into the details of execution, I could imagine some of my frail and vulnerable residents from Kebun Baru running into difficulties.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In theory, they could continue to receive hardcopies of the bills if they opt out.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But this is only if the opt-out process is properly designed.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: My concern is if they are asked to opt out electronically or if the opt-out instruction is buried in the small prints in the property tax notices.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: And worse comes to worst, if the process is not noticed by their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask IRAS to clarify on their proposed framework for implementing this.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Will it be implemented immediately to all property taxpayers?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Will there be an educational effort to help property taxpayers understand that?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: In short, is IRAS considering ways to strike a balance between efficiency and inclusiveness, not just for the Property Tax Bill's amendments today, but also for the other tax Bills put forward today?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I would also like to make a broader point about our move towards a Smart Nation.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: While I share the Government's goal in doing so, it is important we do so in an inclusive way.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: By "inclusive", I hope our Government actively creates alternatives that are cheap, efficient and simple to use.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: If a retiree or a low-income individual is expected to use his or her smartphone to do an electronic transaction, then, (a) he or she must be able to afford a smart phone, even if it is a second-hand one.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: But unfortunately, this cost is not always factored into our social assistance framework; (b) he or she must be able to afford the data-plan, because free wi-fi signal is not always present in all public places and the sign-on process is currently cumbersome.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure that once we implement Smart Nation, we will think through all these applications and these executional bottlenecks, but I hope that our Government can consider all these issues about digital inclusiveness because we must leave no Singaporeans behind as we move towards a digital future.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: One way the Government can do so is for the Smart Nation Office to closely consult the Ministry of Social and Family Development and the various voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) during the design phase while embarking on the digitisation process.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these concerns, I support this Bill as a necessary step to improve our tax system.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill also provides IRAS with further enforcement powers to do their duties, but some of which may be considered slightly intrusive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To address this issue, allow me to seek some clarifications on this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This gives IRAS the ability to gain access to a wide variety of resources, as it will now be able to acquire any devices and documents it requires.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are powers which some might consider to be excessive and a breach of privacy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: People who are under investigation or those who have information regarding the investigation will also be obliged to be personally examined.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that section 64A is similar to the new section 65B in the proposed Income Tax (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, commentators have raised the point that while authorities may need to conduct in-depth investigations on cash transactions of businesses, the case is very different for property tax investigations, where data is widely available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister provide some justification for the empowerment of IRAS, specifically for property tax investigations?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Further, could we also then anticipate similar enforcement powers for all other forms of taxes in the future?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also refer to the amendments of section 56 to increase penalties for hindering or obstructing the Comptroller, Chief Assessor or IRAS officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister provide more details on why this was not included and whether it will be conducting further public consultation on this?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is clear that all four Members support digitalisation but, at the same time, are concerned that people should not be left behind, especially those who are not very IT-savvy or able to deal with digitalisation, and this does the Members credit.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Henry Kwek had asked whether there will be a staged rollout for the opt-out approach for digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah had also asked whether the elderly group will be targeted by the opt-out approach for digital tax notices, and Ms Thanaletchmi has suggested that options for hardcopy tax notices be available, especially for the less IT-savvy residents.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All these are valid concerns and they are concerns which IRAS and MOF looked at as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In this journey to Smart Nation, we will move forward in ways that make transacting with the Government more convenient for our citizens.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But we will also help those who are less digitally ready.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The reason for this is because individuals are familiar with transacting digitally with IRAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, 97% of individuals who file their income tax returns do so electronically through the IRAS My Tax Portal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, let me now deal, first, with the individuals and the residential property owners.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Specifically, IRAS will start with individuals who own residential properties and who have provided their mobile numbers to IRAS, such as through IRAS' My Tax Portal typically.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They would also be aware of this initiative through IRAS' educational efforts to publicise this opt-out approach for digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These individual owners of residential properties would be requested to indicate if they wish to opt out of digital tax notices and thus continue receiving hardcopy tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If they do not opt out from receiving digital tax notices, then IRAS will notify them via short message service (SMS) from November 2017 when the digital tax notices of Property Tax are ready for viewing on the IRAS My Tax Portal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The SMS will also indicate the amount of property tax due in 2018 and the payment due date.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These individuals can log in to their accounts on the IRAS My Tax Portal to view their digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For individuals who have opted out of digital tax notices in October 2017, they will continue to receive hardcopy tax notices from November 2017 for their 2018 property tax.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As with previous years, IRAS will be sending SMS reminders around mid-January 2018 to taxpayers if payment has not been received.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These SMS reminders apply as well to individual owners of residential properties on digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If an individual owner of a residential property on digital tax notice has still not paid by the payment due date, IRAS will issue a hardcopy tax notice then and give the taxpayer sufficient time for payment.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I move on now to those who have not provided their mobile numbers to IRAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In other words, they currently do not transact with IRAS digitally.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Individuals who own residential properties and who have not provided their mobile numbers to IRAS will continue to receive hardcopy tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: They will thus not be receiving the hardcopy opt out letters in October 2017.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Instead, as per previous years, they will receive the hardcopy tax notices from November 2017 for the property tax payable in 2018.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is because they either do not have to pay property tax or are less likely to have their mobile numbers registered with IRAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: IRAS will continue to increase the mobile number database by complementing IRAS current database with the mobile numbers of SingPass two-factor authentication-ready taxpayers to extend the benefits of digital tax notices to other taxpayers in subsequent years.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in other words, phased approach, we take into account those who are elderly and, as the years move on, we will try to add more and more on to the digital database.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In the next phase, IRAS will roll out the digital property tax notices for businesses, including small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and microenterprises.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These businesses can also opt out of digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah had expressed concern about the ability of SMEs and microenterprises to cope with digital tax notices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, GST-registered businesses are already required to e-file the GST returns which are usually filed every quarter through IRAS' My Tax Portal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: E-filing of corporate tax returns will be made compulsory, again in a phased approach, from the year of assessment 2018 to 2020.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: All companies, including SMEs and microenterprises, also e-file their annual returns to the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If businesses have been using agents to handle their accounting and tax matters for them, the agent will be able to handle the digital tax notices as well.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Er Dr Lee asked where the onus lies if a notice for payment from IRAS lands in the taxpayer's email spam folder.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: She also asked how taxpayers can be assured that the notifications and digital tax notices are, indeed, from IRAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Instead, this document will be accessible through IRAS' My Tax Portal.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Thus, taxpayers can be assured that the notices are, indeed, from IRAS.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We appreciate Members' feedback for the opt-out approach for digital tax notices, and IRAS will continue to provide support for taxpayers who are less digitally ready.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With more specialised buildings being developed in Singapore, properties' specific data which is required to effectively assess the property tax may not be widely available.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: With increased incidents with uncooperative taxpayers, IRAS requires more powers to properly assess property tax due.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The amendments will allow IRAS officers to more effectively deal with uncooperative taxpayers and further strengthen the culture of compliance.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This will make it operationally easier for IRAS officers who might have to carry out a joint investigation involving different tax types.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Further, while data may be perceived to be more widely available for property tax assessments as opposed to other tax types, such as income tax or GST, criminal investigations require investigators to gather adequate evidence, including direct and circumstantial evidence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Investigation powers are, therefore, required under the Property Tax Act to equip IRAS investigators to do their job properly.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The enhancement and penalties are in line with the penalties for other tax types and will send a clear signal to the taxpayer community on IRAS' stand against hindering and obstructing.
